claim: Reachable configurations are in bijection with monotone paths from (1,n) to (m,1), hence are counted by binomial(m+n-2,m-1).
reasoning: Initially the empty cells are the last column and last row, a path with word D^(m-1)L^(n-1). If the empties form a monotone path, a legal move sees the path segment (i,j+1)->(i+1,j+1)->(i+1,j), i.e. DL, and replaces it by (i,j+1)->(i,j)->(i+1,j), i.e. LD. Conversely every DL corner has its fourth cell outside the path and therefore occupied, so the swap is legal. Every word in D,L with fixed multiplicities is obtainable from the initial sorted word by adjacent swaps DL->LD. Distinct words give distinct empty-square sets and configurations.

claim: The full original target statement was accepted with answer binomial(m+n-2,m-1).
